question: A 2-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 3-minute episode of a tonic-clonic seizure. The parents deny any previous history of seizure involving the patient or the family. Physical examination reveals an afebrile, well-groomed, and playful appearance, with normal vital signs. The patient carries a pink birthmark on the right side of her face extending from the forehead to the zygomatic arch. Which of the following findings is most likely on a head CT of this patient?

enhanced_information: The most likely finding on a head CT of this patient with a pink birthmark on the right side of her face and a tonic-clonic seizure is a prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification, consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 2-year-old girl with a facial birthmark resembling a port-wine stain and a recent seizure episode is suggestive of Sturge-Weber syndrome. This condition is characterized by a facial capillary malformation (port-wine stain) and neurological abnormalities, including seizures. A common radiological finding in Sturge-Weber syndrome is intracranial calcifications, often described as 'tram-track' calcifications, which are typically found in the cortical and subcortical regions. Therefore, the most likely finding on a head CT would be prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification.
